answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network maps identities onto an interconnected trust trellis, enforcing cryptographic stake burning for validation. When an attacker creates multiple identities, the required burned stake scales as a superlinear function, O(k^2), plunging their capital efficiency to its absolute nadir. This economic friction carves an unbridgeable cost canyon, rendering large-scale identity replication mathematically unprofitable.
